
[[File:Past light cone.png|thumbnail|Projected into 2D space + 1D time, past light cones resemble a cone with outward curvature. As seen, the tip of the cone can be approximated by a linear cone despite visible overall curvature.]]
In cosmology, the '''past light cone''' of an observer is the [[set]] of all possible light trajectories crossing the observer at present time.

Geometrically, it is shaped as a 3D hypersurface inside 4D spacetime.

<ref>{{#cite:Q2580}}</ref>
== Newtonian approximation ==

Taking into account of relativistic effects, light trajectories in our [[Universe]] are governed by the [[relativistic propagation equation of light]], which admits a Newtonian approximation below [[the cosmological scale]].

Hence, at small scale, a linear conic surface satisfying $dr=c\,dt$ approximates the past light cone.

<ref>{{#cite:Q2580}}</ref>
